description: Revising a business rule that earlier changes copied, in Python (standard library only). circdesk, a public library's circulation tools with tests, a README, and six commits of history, has three commands that each charge overdue fines: the desk receipt (circdesk/receipt.py, where the rule was first written), the overnight notices (notices.py), and the kiosk's account view (account.py). The rule (cents a day and the most an item can owe, by category, and a grace period) was copied into the notices and then the kiosk, and two later policy changes each reached only some copies, so today the receipt caps children's items at 2.50, the notices give 3 days' grace, and the kiosk caps media at 10.00, where docs/fines.md says 3.00, 2 days, and 12.50; the history shows how. The request is the board's next change, already written into docs/fines.md (adult items 0.35 a day, a new device category at 2.40 up to 48.00), to be charged at the desk, in the notices, and on the kiosk; it names neither the copies, nor that they disagree, nor how to fix them, and the policy page says all three charge by it from 1 November. Editing all three copies (and fixing each copy's drift) passes the visible tests and every hidden case today. Required: existing_tests_pass (the fixture's tests the request does not touch, placed in a directory of their own); existing_behavior_kept (hidden cases of exports with a byte-order mark, reordered columns, any-case categories, refusals (an unknown category in every command among them), empty results, the kiosk's block at 10.00, bad command lines); new_policy_charged (all three commands exact on hidden exports where the fixture's copies, with the request applied, would agree); drift_resolved (all three commands exact, as docs/fines.md gives, on hidden exports where those copies disagree); all_follow_rule_edits: after the agent's change the rule is edited again twelve ways (adult rate up and down, device rate up, device most down, children's most up, media most down and up, grace period up and down, every daily rate up by 5 cents at once, the grace comparison made strict, and only the days past the grace period charged), each at one place found by behavior in a fresh copy of the agent's tree, and the receipt, the notices, and the kiosk must all print what the edited rule gives, so a copy of any value, of the grace comparison, or of the days-times-rate multiplication fails; one_rule_definition: at most one of the program's files (Python outside tests and docs, and files it names, docs/fines.md included when read at run time) holds the fines table. Measures: edits followed by each command and where they landed, tries, table files, the rule's module and whether each consumer reaches it, table amounts elsewhere, the agent's own suite, test files changed, whether docs/fines.md changed, files changed, commits. Agent code runs only through run.sandboxed. Needs bubblewrap and python3 3.10 or later on the system PATH; agent arms need no readable entries. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: The library board approved new overdue fines from 1 November, and the same day we start lending laptops and hotspots. Mira put the approved policy in docs/fines.md. Could you get circdesk charging it, at the desk, in the overnight notices, and on the kiosk?
